entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hori I was the High Priest of Ptah at the end of Ramesses II's reign, succeeding Neferronpet in office. He played a crucial role in the administrative and religious life of ancient Egypt during the late 13th century BCE.

As High Priest, Hori oversaw the construction of several temples, including the Temple of Ptah in Memphis, which became a center of worship for the god Ptah. He also participated in the cultic practices and rituals associated with Ptah, ensuring the continued vitality of the deity in Egyptian religious life.

Hori's tenure as High Priest coincided with significant events in ancient Egyptian history, including the reign of Pharaoh Ramses II (1279-1213 BCE) and the rise of the New Kingdom period. His leadership during this time helped maintain stability and continuity in the face of external threats from neighboring powers.

Despite his importance, Hori's legacy has not been extensively documented by modern historians, making him a lesser-known figure in the annals of ancient Egyptian history. Nevertheless, his contributions to the religious and administrative life of Egypt during a critical period warrant further study and recognition.
